text:
mika: Heads-up: seeing a weird backoff-reset race in the Kotlin SDK sample app when token refresh races with retry/backoff. Repro steps in repo.

rohit: what's the symptom?

mika: under flaky auth service we trigger a refresh mid-backoff; when refresh completes our retry interceptor resets the backoff state for that endpoint globally, which causes a bunch of concurrent callers to immediately retry instead of respecting jittered backoff. Net effect: small transient auth blip -> burst of retries -> downstream rate limits and more 401s.

anya: can you paste minimal retry state snippet?

mika: snippet: `class BackoffState { var attempts = 0; fun nextDelay() = base * (2.pow(attempts++)) ; fun reset() { attempts = 0 } }` and we call reset() after successful refresh.

kevin: resetting shared state on any successful refresh is dangerous if multiple in-flight requests share the same BackoffState instance. You need per-call backoff or a coordinated reset that only unblocks callers that caused the refresh.

rohit: we saw similar in prod when using a singleton retry cache. Fix options: 1) give each call its own backoff instance, 2) track backoff keyed by call id (not endpoint) and only reset the exact key, or 3) use a token-refresh singleflight that returns a Result that callers can observe and then individually reset their own attempt counters.

anya: for the sample app I pushed a small change: switch BackoffState to be immutable per attempt and implement singleflight refresh via a suspend mutex so only one network refresh occurs. On success we publish the new token but callers keep their local attempt counters so they keep exponential spacing. PR includes test that simulates 50 concurrent calls and flaky auth.

kevin: please add a docs blurb: "Backoff + Auth: avoid shared mutable backoff state" and include the singleflight pattern example. Also add a runbook note: look for a spike of retries immediately after a token refresh, and server-side rate-limit responses.

mika: added PR #5134 with sample changes, tests, and docs. CI: build-bot: runs unit + small emu test.

build-bot: CI passed on jvm and emulator-23. Next: validate on Android 14 emulator.

rohit: thanks. Also note in docs the okhttp dispatcher caveat and that retry scheduling should avoid blocking OkHttp threads (use a scheduler/executor).

mika: agreed, will include a short note about scheduling retries off the network dispatcher. Closing after alpha validation. :thumbsup:
